segments.text: "Welcome to the Daily Robotics Brief, I'm your host.
August 18th, 2026.
In robotics news, Serve Robotics is expanding its delivery network, while All Three Major US Airlines have banned humanoids due to battery fire risks.
Meanwhile, Samsung is pushing its humanoid development forward with a new dedicated unit and AI advancements.
We'll dive into these stories and more, bringing you the latest in robotics today."
From Robotics & Automation News, "Serve Robotics adds Grubhub to delivery network as Diligent rolls out Moxi 2.0".
Serve Robotics is expanding its autonomous delivery network by partnering with Grubhub, adding a third major delivery platform to its network alongside Uber Eats and DoorDash.
The Grubhub agreement is being rolled out in Chicago, Los Angeles, and Alexandria, Virginia, with over 100 participating restaurants in Chicago and nearly 200 in Los Angeles.
Diligent Robotics, meanwhile, is launching its Moxi 2.0 mobile manipulation robot in hospitals across the US, with initial deployments in Chicago, Los Angeles, and Washington, DC.
The Moxi 2.0 robot is designed to assist with tasks such as medication delivery and patient transport.

This expansion marks significant developments in the autonomous delivery and robotics industries, highlighting the growing demand for advanced delivery solutions and the increasing adoption of mobile manipulation robots in healthcare settings.
From Humanoids Daily, "No Robots Allowed: All Three Major US Airlines Ban Humanoids Over Battery Fire Risks".

US airlines American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, United Airlines, and Southwest Airlines have banned humanoid robots from being brought onto flights due to safety concerns over battery fire risks, which pose a catastrophic threat in a confined cabin.

The Federal Aviation Administration had previously established a maximum allowance of 160 Wh for lithium-ion batteries, but humanoid robots often exceed this limit, rendering them unsuitable for in-flight use.
The airlines' decision to ban humanoids closes a loophole and clarifies that they do not qualify as emotional support devices.
From Humanoids Daily, "Samsung Accelerates In-House Humanoid Development with Dedicated RX Unit and World Model AI."

Samsung has established a dedicated Robotics eXperience Business Promotion Office directly reporting to CEO TM Roh, and has hired former Hyundai executive Lee Dong-geon to steer robotics strategy, as the company accelerates its in-house humanoid development with a dedicated RX unit and integration of internal manufacturing data, custom hardware, and foundation AI models.
This centralized effort combines Samsung's proprietary Gauss foundation model with new "world models" designed to simulate physical dynamics before execution, building a physical AI software stack.
Samsung's humanoid initiative marks a significant step forward in its AI development capabilities, as the company seeks to establish itself as a major player in the robotics industry.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Never miss a backport again — automatic ABI checking for ROS 2 core repos (prototype ready)".
A prototype has been developed to automatically check the ABI compatibility of ROS 2 core repository fixes, eliminating the need for manual backporting efforts.
This prototype utilizes two GitHub Actions, libabigail-action and ros2-abi-action, which compare shared libraries using libabigail and apply the REP-0009 policy for released distros and rolling.
The tool can be integrated into the ROS 2 core repos and potentially shared with community packages, with feedback and concerns welcomed.
The development of this prototype marks a significant advancement in the efficiency of ROS 2 maintenance.
From Humanoids Daily, "Schaeffler Cracks the Cost Bottleneck: Formed Strain Wave Gearboxes Target 2027 Mass Production".
Schaeffler has introduced a new high-speed forming process for strain wave gearboxes, significantly reducing component costs by over 25% and material consumption by over 75%.

This breakthrough was achieved through the development of a novel forming technology that enables precise control over the gear's shape and structure, resulting in improved manufacturability and reduced waste.
The new process will be implemented in time for mass production in 2027 in Germany, prior to a global expansion to support humanoid robotics partners.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Building Networks That Can Keep Up With Modern Automation"

, this story highlights the critical need for industrial networks to adapt to increasing automation, revealing that a network planning approach that prioritizes traffic patterns over individual devices is crucial to maintaining predictability as equipment and production requirements evolve.

Industry experts have found that by mapping traffic patterns in addition to device placement, teams can create more resilient networks that can handle the simultaneous production and consumption of data by various devices.

This approach, which involves analyzing network topology and identifying potential bottlenecks, enables the creation of a network that can maintain stability even in the face of equipment failures or unexpected changes in production demands.
As a result, teams can minimize downtime and ensure that diagnostic processes can be completed efficiently.

This shift in network planning approach has significant implications for the AI and tech industry, as it underscores the growing importance of adaptability and flexibility in industrial automation systems.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Is Shipyard Welding the Right First Job for Humanoid Robots?"
This project aims to create a humanoid robot capable of performing long, linear welds in shipyards.

Persona AI has developed a humanoid robot specifically designed for this task, leveraging the robot's ability to perform millimeter-scale repeated motions, a skill robots excel at, particularly over long periods.
The company has chosen shipyards as the initial target due to their industrial environment, which reduces safety concerns for the robot.
The robot can work on the ground, overhead, and through portholes, allowing for a comprehensive range of tasks.
By creating high-fidelity simulations and collecting demonstration data, Persona AI plans to expand its applications to grinding and painting, further enhancing the robot's capabilities.
From Robohub, "Intermittent swimming promotes the energy efficiency of fish-like robot movements,"
researchers have developed a larval zebrafish-inspired robotic platform, known as ZBot, to investigate the energy efficiency of intermittent swimming compared to continuous swimming.
The team found that intermittent bout-and-glide swimming reduces energy consumption across all achievable velocities, especially in viscous fluid regimes.

By analyzing the energy transfer between the actuator and kinematic tail movements, the researchers proposed the "actuator efficiency" hypothesis, suggesting that intermittent swimming enhances the efficiency of energy transfer, allowing actuators to operate in more energy-efficient regimes.
"Thanks for joining me on the robotic revolution!
It's been a wild ride today, as Serve Robotics just served up a juicy partnership with Grubhub and Diligent rolled out its Moxi 2.0 - talk about efficient delivery!
Until next time, keep on charging!"
